standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma producing a section of a finite etale cover of a closed subscheme of a normal affine scheme with absolutely algebraically closed function field

core_obligations: Translate the class into a torsor (proof lines 14431-14436): a class in H^1(Z_etale, M) corresponds to an M-torsor F on Z_etale, and such a torsor is clearly a finite locally constant sheaf.

Represent the torsor by a scheme (proof lines 14436-14439): by the representation lemma the torsor F is representable by a scheme V finite etale over Z, and V -> Z is surjective because a torsor is locally trivial.

Find a section and conclude (proof lines 14439-14441): the cited lemma on finite etale covers of a closed subscheme of a normal affine scheme with algebraically closed function field gives a section of V -> Z, so the torsor is trivial and the class vanishes, whence H^1(Z_etale, M) = 0.
proof_roadmap: Replace the cohomology class by an M-torsor on the closed subscheme.
Represent that torsor by a finite etale scheme over the closed subscheme.
Use the existence of a section to split the torsor and kill the class.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a normal integral affine scheme X with separably closed function field and a closed subscheme Z, the first etale cohomology of Z with coefficients in a finite abelian group vanishes (statement lines 14424-14429). The proof (proof lines 14431-14442) translates the class into a torsor, represents it by a finite etale scheme and uses the existence of a section of that cover to trivialize the torsor. H2: a three-step translation with three inputs, written out in full.
